// reduction 
template<typename T>
__inline__ __device__ T warpReduceSum(T val)
{
#pragma unroll
    for (int mask = 16; mask > 0; mask >>= 1)
        val = add(val, __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, val, mask, 32));
    return val;
}

/* Calculate the sum of all elements in a block */
template<typename T>
__inline__ __device__ T blockReduceSum(T val)
{
    static __shared__ T shared[32];
    int lane = threadIdx.x & 0x1f;
    int wid = threadIdx.x >> 5;

    val = warpReduceSum<T>(val);

    if (lane == 0)
        shared[wid] = val;

    __syncthreads();

    val = (threadIdx.x < (blockDim.x / 32)) ? shared[lane] : (T)(0.0f);
    val = warpReduceSum<T>(val);

    return val;
}

template<typename T>
__global__ void addBiasResidualPostLayerNormV2(
          T* out,
    const T* __restrict__ input,
    const T* __restrict__ bias,
    const T* __restrict__ gamma,
    const T* __restrict__ beta,
    const float layernorm_eps,
    const int n)
{
  using T2             = typename TypeConverter<T>::Type;
  const int        ite = 4;
  const int        tid = threadIdx.x;
  const int        bid = blockIdx.x;
  __shared__ float s_mean;
  __shared__ float s_variance;
  float            mean     = 0.0f;
  float            variance = 0.0f;
  T2               local_out_half2[ite];

  T2*       out_ptr   = (T2*)out;
  const T2* input_ptr = (const T2*)input;
  const T2* bias_ptr  = (const T2*)bias;
  const T2* gamma_ptr = (const T2*)gamma;
  const T2* beta_ptr  = (const T2*)beta;

  T2 sum = floatToType2<T2>(0.0f);

  // ite = 4 and blockDim.x = n / 8
  // When n = 1024, blockDim.x = 128
  // col_id range: [0-127], [128-255], [256-383], [384-511]
  // block stride = n / 2 = 512
#pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < ite; i++) {
    int col_id         = i * blockDim.x + tid;
    int id             = bid * n / 2 + col_id;
    local_out_half2[i] = add(out_ptr[id], input_ptr[id], bias_ptr[col_id]);
    sum                = add(sum, local_out_half2[i]);
  }

  mean = blockReduceSum<float>(typeToFloat(__hadd(sum.x , sum.y)));
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_mean = mean / n;
  }
  __syncthreads();

  float var      = 0.0f;
  T2    s_mean_2 = floatToType2<T2>(s_mean);

#pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < ite; i++) {
    local_out_half2[i] = sub(local_out_half2[i], s_mean_2);
    float v1           = typeToFloat(local_out_half2[i].x);
    float v2           = typeToFloat(local_out_half2[i].y);
    var += v1 * v1 + v2 * v2;
  }

  variance = blockReduceSum<float>(var);
  if (tid == 0) {
    s_variance = rsqrtf(variance / n + layernorm_eps);
  }
  __syncthreads();

  T2 s_var_2 = floatToType2<T2>(s_variance);
#pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < ite; i++) {
    int col_id  = i * blockDim.x + tid;
    int id      = bid * n / 2 + col_id;
    out_ptr[id] = fma(local_out_half2[i], s_var_2,
                      gamma_ptr[col_id], beta_ptr[col_id]);
  }
}

template<typename T, int N>
__global__ void addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm(
          T* out, 
    const T* __restrict__ input,
    const T* __restrict__ bias,
    const T* __restrict__ gamma,
    const T* __restrict__ beta,
    const float layernorm_eps,
    const int n)
{
  __shared__ float s_mean;
  __shared__ float s_variance;
  float            mean     = 0.0f;
  float            variance = 0.0f;
  float            local_out_cache[N];

#pragma unroll N
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x, i = 0; idx < n && i < N; ++i) {
    float local_out = typeToFloat(add(out[blockIdx.x * n + idx], input[blockIdx.x * n + idx], bias[idx]));
    mean += local_out;
    // save local_out to local_out_cache to save some recompute
    local_out_cache[i] = local_out;
    idx += blockDim.x;
  }

  mean = blockReduceSum<float>(mean);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_mean = mean / n;
  }
  __syncthreads();

#pragma unroll N
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x, i = 0; idx < n && i < N; ++i) {
    float local_out = local_out_cache[i];
    variance += (local_out - s_mean) * (local_out - s_mean);
    idx += blockDim.x;
  }
  variance = blockReduceSum<float>(variance);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_variance = variance / n + layernorm_eps;
  }
  __syncthreads();

#pragma unroll N
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x, i = 0; idx < n && i < N; ++i) {
    float local_out = local_out_cache[i];
    out[blockIdx.x * n + idx] =
      floatToType<T>(((local_out - s_mean) * rsqrtf(s_variance)) * typeToFloat(gamma[idx]) + typeToFloat(beta[idx]));
    idx += blockDim.x;
  }
}

template<typename T>
__global__ void generalAddBiasResidualPostLayerNorm(
          T* out, 
    const T* __restrict__ input,
    const T* __restrict__ bias,
    const T* __restrict__ gamma,
    const T* __restrict__ beta,
    const float layernorm_eps,
    const int n)
{
  using T2 = typename TypeConverter<T>::Type;
  __shared__ float s_mean;
  __shared__ float s_variance;
  float            mean     = 0.0f;
  float            variance = 0.0f;

  T2*       out_ptr   = (T2*)out;
  const T2* input_ptr = (const T2*)input;
  const T2* bias_ptr  = (const T2*)bias;
  const T2* gamma_ptr = (const T2*)gamma;
  const T2* beta_ptr  = (const T2*)beta;

  float local_out = 0.0f;
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < n / 2; idx += blockDim.x) {
    int    id            = blockIdx.x * n / 2 + idx;
    T2     tmp           = add(add(out_ptr[id], input_ptr[id]), bias_ptr[idx]);
    float2 local_out_fp2 = type2ToFloat2(tmp);
    local_out += local_out_fp2.x;
    local_out += local_out_fp2.y;
    // save tmp to out_ptr to save some recomputation
    out_ptr[id] = tmp;
  }

  mean = blockReduceSum<float>(local_out);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_mean = mean / n;
  }
  __syncthreads();

  for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < n / 2; idx += blockDim.x) {
    int    id            = blockIdx.x * n / 2 + idx;
    float2 local_out_fp2 = type2ToFloat2(out_ptr[id]);
    variance += (local_out_fp2.x - s_mean) * (local_out_fp2.x - s_mean);
    variance += (local_out_fp2.y - s_mean) * (local_out_fp2.y - s_mean);
  }

  variance = blockReduceSum<float>(variance);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_variance = rsqrtf(variance / n + layernorm_eps);
  }
  __syncthreads();

  for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < n / 2; idx += blockDim.x) {
    int    id            = blockIdx.x * n / 2 + idx;
    float2 local_out_fp2 = type2ToFloat2(out_ptr[id]);
    float2 gamma_val     = type2ToFloat2(gamma_ptr[idx]);
    float2 beta_val      = type2ToFloat2(beta_ptr[idx]);
    local_out_fp2.x      = (local_out_fp2.x - s_mean) * s_variance * gamma_val.x + beta_val.x;
    local_out_fp2.y      = (local_out_fp2.y - s_mean) * s_variance * gamma_val.y + beta_val.y;
    out_ptr[id]          = float2ToType2<T2>(local_out_fp2);
  }
}

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <random>
#include <cuda.h>
#include <cuda_fp16.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include "kernels.h"

// V: version
template<typename T, int V>
void invokeAddBiasResidualLayerNorm(
          T*     out,
    const T*     input,
    const T*     bias,
    const T*     gamma,
    const T*     beta,
    const float  layernorm_eps,
    int          m,
    int          n)
{
  dim3 grid(m);
  dim3 block(std::min(n, 256));

  if (V == 2) { // assume n % 8 == 0
    addBiasResidualPostLayerNormV2<T><<<grid, n / 8>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
  }
  else {
    int num_trips = (n + block.x - 1) / block.x;
    if (num_trips == 1) {
      addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T, 1>
        <<<grid, block>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
    }
    else if (num_trips == 2) {
      addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T, 2>
        <<<grid, block>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
    }
    else {
      generalAddBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T>
        <<<grid, block>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
    }
  }
}

template<typename T, int V>
void layer(int repeat) {

  const int m = 4096;  // batch size

  int dim[] = {256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192};

  for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(dim) / sizeof(int); i++) {

    std::mt19937 gen (19937);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dis(0.f, 1.f);

    // n-dimensional data
    const int n = dim[i]; 
    const int input_size = m * n;
    const int output_size = m * n;
    const int input_size_bytes = input_size * sizeof(T);
    const int output_size_bytes = output_size * sizeof(T);
    const int bias_size_bytes = n * sizeof(T);
    const int beta_size_bytes = n * sizeof(T);
    const int gamma_size_bytes = n * sizeof(T);

    T *h_input = (T*) malloc (input_size_bytes);
    T *h_output = (T*) malloc (output_size_bytes);
    T *h_bias = (T*) malloc (bias_size_bytes);
    T *h_gamma = (T*) malloc (gamma_size_bytes);
    T *h_beta = (T*) malloc (beta_size_bytes);

    for (int i = 0; i < input_size; i++) {
      h_input[i] = (T) dis(gen);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      h_bias[i] = (T) dis(gen);
      h_gamma[i] = (T) dis(gen);
      h_beta[i] = (T) dis(gen);
    }

    float layernorm_eps = 1e-6;
    T *d_input, *d_output, *d_bias, *d_gamma, *d_beta;
    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_input, input_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_input, h_input, input_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_output,  output_size_bytes);
    cudaMemset(d_output,  0, output_size_bytes); // need to reset output

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_bias,  bias_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_bias, h_bias, bias_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_gamma,  gamma_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_gamma, h_gamma, gamma_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_beta,  beta_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_beta, h_beta, beta_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaDeviceSynchronize();
    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++) {
      invokeAddBiasResidualLayerNorm<T, V>
          (d_output, d_input, d_bias, d_gamma, d_beta, layernorm_eps, m, n);
    }
    cudaDeviceSynchronize();
    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
    printf("Average execution time of AddBiasResidualLayerNorm (%d x %d): %f (us)\n",
           m, n, (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

    cudaMemcpy(h_output, d_output, output_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

    float s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < output_size; i++)
      s += float(h_output[i]);

    printf("Checksum = %f\n", s / (m * n));
    
    cudaFree(d_input);
    cudaFree(d_output);
    cudaFree(d_bias);
    cudaFree(d_gamma);
    cudaFree(d_beta);

    free(h_input);
    free(h_output);
    free(h_bias);
    free(h_gamma);
    free(h_beta);
  }
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 2) {
    printf("Usage: %s <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  const int repeat = atoi(argv[1]);
  printf("---------------- float16 (version 1) -------------\n");
  layer<half, 1>(repeat);
  printf("---------------- float16 (version 2) -------------\n");
  layer<half, 2>(repeat);

  printf("---------------- bfloat16 (version 1) -------------\n");
  layer<__nv_bfloat16, 1>(repeat);
  printf("---------------- bfloat16 (version 2) -------------\n");
  layer<__nv_bfloat16, 2>(repeat);
  return 0;
}

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them. If SASS is provided, use the global load and store instructions in SASS, especially LDG and STG, to identify the actual global-memory traffic generated by execution.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.

Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.
- Use SASS as the primary low-level evidence for executed memory behavior when available, and map SASS back to source when that helps explain hidden or optimized memory behavior.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

// reduction 
template<typename T>
__inline__ __device__ T warpReduceSum(T val)
{
#pragma unroll
    for (int mask = 16; mask > 0; mask >>= 1)
        val = add(val, __shfl_xor_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, val, mask, 32));
    return val;
}

/* Calculate the sum of all elements in a block */
template<typename T>
__inline__ __device__ T blockReduceSum(T val)
{
    static __shared__ T shared[32];
    int lane = threadIdx.x & 0x1f;
    int wid = threadIdx.x >> 5;

    val = warpReduceSum<T>(val);

    if (lane == 0)
        shared[wid] = val;

    __syncthreads();

    val = (threadIdx.x < (blockDim.x / 32)) ? shared[lane] : (T)(0.0f);
    val = warpReduceSum<T>(val);

    return val;
}

template<typename T>
__global__ void addBiasResidualPostLayerNormV2(
          T* out,
    const T* __restrict__ input,
    const T* __restrict__ bias,
    const T* __restrict__ gamma,
    const T* __restrict__ beta,
    const float layernorm_eps,
    const int n)
{
  using T2             = typename TypeConverter<T>::Type;
  const int        ite = 4;
  const int        tid = threadIdx.x;
  const int        bid = blockIdx.x;
  __shared__ float s_mean;
  __shared__ float s_variance;
  float            mean     = 0.0f;
  float            variance = 0.0f;
  T2               local_out_half2[ite];

  T2*       out_ptr   = (T2*)out;
  const T2* input_ptr = (const T2*)input;
  const T2* bias_ptr  = (const T2*)bias;
  const T2* gamma_ptr = (const T2*)gamma;
  const T2* beta_ptr  = (const T2*)beta;

  T2 sum = floatToType2<T2>(0.0f);

  // ite = 4 and blockDim.x = n / 8
  // When n = 1024, blockDim.x = 128
  // col_id range: [0-127], [128-255], [256-383], [384-511]
  // block stride = n / 2 = 512
#pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < ite; i++) {
    int col_id         = i * blockDim.x + tid;
    int id             = bid * n / 2 + col_id;
    local_out_half2[i] = add(out_ptr[id], input_ptr[id], bias_ptr[col_id]);
    sum                = add(sum, local_out_half2[i]);
  }

  mean = blockReduceSum<float>(typeToFloat(__hadd(sum.x , sum.y)));
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_mean = mean / n;
  }
  __syncthreads();

  float var      = 0.0f;
  T2    s_mean_2 = floatToType2<T2>(s_mean);

#pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < ite; i++) {
    local_out_half2[i] = sub(local_out_half2[i], s_mean_2);
    float v1           = typeToFloat(local_out_half2[i].x);
    float v2           = typeToFloat(local_out_half2[i].y);
    var += v1 * v1 + v2 * v2;
  }

  variance = blockReduceSum<float>(var);
  if (tid == 0) {
    s_variance = rsqrtf(variance / n + layernorm_eps);
  }
  __syncthreads();

  T2 s_var_2 = floatToType2<T2>(s_variance);
#pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < ite; i++) {
    int col_id  = i * blockDim.x + tid;
    int id      = bid * n / 2 + col_id;
    out_ptr[id] = fma(local_out_half2[i], s_var_2,
                      gamma_ptr[col_id], beta_ptr[col_id]);
  }
}

template<typename T, int N>
__global__ void addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm(
          T* out, 
    const T* __restrict__ input,
    const T* __restrict__ bias,
    const T* __restrict__ gamma,
    const T* __restrict__ beta,
    const float layernorm_eps,
    const int n)
{
  __shared__ float s_mean;
  __shared__ float s_variance;
  float            mean     = 0.0f;
  float            variance = 0.0f;
  float            local_out_cache[N];

#pragma unroll N
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x, i = 0; idx < n && i < N; ++i) {
    float local_out = typeToFloat(add(out[blockIdx.x * n + idx], input[blockIdx.x * n + idx], bias[idx]));
    mean += local_out;
    // save local_out to local_out_cache to save some recompute
    local_out_cache[i] = local_out;
    idx += blockDim.x;
  }

  mean = blockReduceSum<float>(mean);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_mean = mean / n;
  }
  __syncthreads();

#pragma unroll N
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x, i = 0; idx < n && i < N; ++i) {
    float local_out = local_out_cache[i];
    variance += (local_out - s_mean) * (local_out - s_mean);
    idx += blockDim.x;
  }
  variance = blockReduceSum<float>(variance);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_variance = variance / n + layernorm_eps;
  }
  __syncthreads();

#pragma unroll N
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x, i = 0; idx < n && i < N; ++i) {
    float local_out = local_out_cache[i];
    out[blockIdx.x * n + idx] =
      floatToType<T>(((local_out - s_mean) * rsqrtf(s_variance)) * typeToFloat(gamma[idx]) + typeToFloat(beta[idx]));
    idx += blockDim.x;
  }
}

template<typename T>
__global__ void generalAddBiasResidualPostLayerNorm(
          T* out, 
    const T* __restrict__ input,
    const T* __restrict__ bias,
    const T* __restrict__ gamma,
    const T* __restrict__ beta,
    const float layernorm_eps,
    const int n)
{
  using T2 = typename TypeConverter<T>::Type;
  __shared__ float s_mean;
  __shared__ float s_variance;
  float            mean     = 0.0f;
  float            variance = 0.0f;

  T2*       out_ptr   = (T2*)out;
  const T2* input_ptr = (const T2*)input;
  const T2* bias_ptr  = (const T2*)bias;
  const T2* gamma_ptr = (const T2*)gamma;
  const T2* beta_ptr  = (const T2*)beta;

  float local_out = 0.0f;
  for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < n / 2; idx += blockDim.x) {
    int    id            = blockIdx.x * n / 2 + idx;
    T2     tmp           = add(add(out_ptr[id], input_ptr[id]), bias_ptr[idx]);
    float2 local_out_fp2 = type2ToFloat2(tmp);
    local_out += local_out_fp2.x;
    local_out += local_out_fp2.y;
    // save tmp to out_ptr to save some recomputation
    out_ptr[id] = tmp;
  }

  mean = blockReduceSum<float>(local_out);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_mean = mean / n;
  }
  __syncthreads();

  for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < n / 2; idx += blockDim.x) {
    int    id            = blockIdx.x * n / 2 + idx;
    float2 local_out_fp2 = type2ToFloat2(out_ptr[id]);
    variance += (local_out_fp2.x - s_mean) * (local_out_fp2.x - s_mean);
    variance += (local_out_fp2.y - s_mean) * (local_out_fp2.y - s_mean);
  }

  variance = blockReduceSum<float>(variance);
  if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
    s_variance = rsqrtf(variance / n + layernorm_eps);
  }
  __syncthreads();

  for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < n / 2; idx += blockDim.x) {
    int    id            = blockIdx.x * n / 2 + idx;
    float2 local_out_fp2 = type2ToFloat2(out_ptr[id]);
    float2 gamma_val     = type2ToFloat2(gamma_ptr[idx]);
    float2 beta_val      = type2ToFloat2(beta_ptr[idx]);
    local_out_fp2.x      = (local_out_fp2.x - s_mean) * s_variance * gamma_val.x + beta_val.x;
    local_out_fp2.y      = (local_out_fp2.y - s_mean) * s_variance * gamma_val.y + beta_val.y;
    out_ptr[id]          = float2ToType2<T2>(local_out_fp2);
  }
}

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <random>
#include <cuda.h>
#include <cuda_fp16.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include "kernels.h"

// V: version
template<typename T, int V>
void invokeAddBiasResidualLayerNorm(
          T*     out,
    const T*     input,
    const T*     bias,
    const T*     gamma,
    const T*     beta,
    const float  layernorm_eps,
    int          m,
    int          n)
{
  dim3 grid(m);
  dim3 block(std::min(n, 256));

  if (V == 2) { // assume n % 8 == 0
    addBiasResidualPostLayerNormV2<T><<<grid, n / 8>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
  }
  else {
    int num_trips = (n + block.x - 1) / block.x;
    if (num_trips == 1) {
      addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T, 1>
        <<<grid, block>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
    }
    else if (num_trips == 2) {
      addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T, 2>
        <<<grid, block>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
    }
    else {
      generalAddBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T>
        <<<grid, block>>>(out, input, bias, gamma, beta, layernorm_eps, n);
    }
  }
}

template<typename T, int V>
void layer(int repeat) {

  const int m = 4096;  // batch size

  int dim[] = {256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192};

  for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(dim) / sizeof(int); i++) {

    std::mt19937 gen (19937);
    std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dis(0.f, 1.f);

    // n-dimensional data
    const int n = dim[i]; 
    const int input_size = m * n;
    const int output_size = m * n;
    const int input_size_bytes = input_size * sizeof(T);
    const int output_size_bytes = output_size * sizeof(T);
    const int bias_size_bytes = n * sizeof(T);
    const int beta_size_bytes = n * sizeof(T);
    const int gamma_size_bytes = n * sizeof(T);

    T *h_input = (T*) malloc (input_size_bytes);
    T *h_output = (T*) malloc (output_size_bytes);
    T *h_bias = (T*) malloc (bias_size_bytes);
    T *h_gamma = (T*) malloc (gamma_size_bytes);
    T *h_beta = (T*) malloc (beta_size_bytes);

    for (int i = 0; i < input_size; i++) {
      h_input[i] = (T) dis(gen);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      h_bias[i] = (T) dis(gen);
      h_gamma[i] = (T) dis(gen);
      h_beta[i] = (T) dis(gen);
    }

    float layernorm_eps = 1e-6;
    T *d_input, *d_output, *d_bias, *d_gamma, *d_beta;
    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_input, input_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_input, h_input, input_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_output,  output_size_bytes);
    cudaMemset(d_output,  0, output_size_bytes); // need to reset output

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_bias,  bias_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_bias, h_bias, bias_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_gamma,  gamma_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_gamma, h_gamma, gamma_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaMalloc((void**)&d_beta,  beta_size_bytes);
    cudaMemcpy(d_beta, h_beta, beta_size_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

    cudaDeviceSynchronize();
    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++) {
      invokeAddBiasResidualLayerNorm<T, V>
          (d_output, d_input, d_bias, d_gamma, d_beta, layernorm_eps, m, n);

prediction.gridSz_explanation: The kernel is launched from `invokeAddBiasResidualLayerNorm` with `dim3 grid(m)` where m=4096. For n=512, num_trips = ceil(512/256) = 2, routing to `addBiasResidualPostLayerNorm<T,2>`. For n=1024, num_trips = ceil(1024/256) = 4, which goes to the `else` branch calling `generalAddBiasResidualPostLayerNorm`. So the first invocation of the target kernel is with m=4096, n=1024, grid=dim3(4096), block=dim3(min(1024,256))=dim3(256).

From SASS: HADD2 (add out+input), HADD2 (add bias) → FP16 ops counted separately.

Per iteration: 4 FP32 ops. Over 2 iterations: 8 FP32 ops per thread.

- First warpReduceSum: 5 FADD per thread × 256 threads = 1280
- Second warpReduceSum: 5 FADD per thread × up to 8 threads (256/32=8 warps, so 8 values loaded, but only first warp of 32 threads participates, with 8 having real values and 24 having zero) = 5×32 = 160 (but 24 threads add zeros, still counted)

Per block for reduce #1: 256×5 + 32×5 = 1440 FADD (approximately, some threads get 0).

F2FP: 0 FP32 ops (conversion).
Per iteration: 6+2+2+4 = 14. Over 2 iterations: 28 per thread.

prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
For n=1024, each block processes one row. Loop 1: reads out_ptr (half2), input_ptr (half2), bias_ptr (half2) — each 4 bytes per half2 element, 512 elements per row for out and input, 512 elements for bias. Per block: out=2048B, input=2048B, bias=2048B. But bias is shared across all 4096 blocks (only 2048B unique), so it's read once from DRAM and cached. Loop 2: reads out_ptr again (just written in loop 1, should be in L1/L2 cache). Loop 3: reads out_ptr, gamma_ptr, beta_ptr. gamma and beta are each 1024 half elements = 2048B, shared across blocks.

Unique data: out array = 4096×1024×2 = 8,388,608 bytes (read+write). input = 8,388,608 bytes (read only). bias = 2048 bytes. gamma = 2048 bytes. beta = 2048 bytes.

Total unique read footprint: input (8,388,608) + out initial read (8,388,608) + bias (2,048) + gamma (2,048) + beta (2,048) = 16,783,360 bytes. The out array is also read back in loops 2 and 3 but from the same addresses written in loop 1, so those reads hit L2/L1 cache for the same block's data.

However, with 4096 blocks and each block writing 2048B to out, the out array written data (8MB) exceeds L2 (6MB), so re-reads of out in loops 2 and 3 within the same block should hit L1 cache (written and read by same block). The initial read of out (which was memset to 0) is 8,388,608 bytes from DRAM.

Total DRAM reads: ~16,781,312 bytes (input 8,388,608 + out 8,388,608 + bias 2,048 + gamma 2,048 + beta 2,048 ≈ 16,783,360). Rounding to cache line granularity.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Loop 1 writes out_ptr: each block writes 512 half2 elements = 2048 bytes. Total: 4096 × 2048 = 8,388,608 bytes. Loop 3 also writes out_ptr: same addresses, same size = 8,388,608 bytes. The total unique write footprint is 8,388,608 bytes (same locations written twice). Since 8MB > 6MB L2 cache, the first set of writes (loop 1) will start getting evicted as later blocks execute. The second set of writes (loop 3) overwrites the same locations. Given the streaming pattern across 4096 blocks, the loop 1 writes will be evicted to DRAM for blocks whose cache lines get evicted before loop 3 of the same block overwrites them. However, within a single block, loops 1, 2, and 3 execute sequentially, so loop 3 overwrites loop 1's data before it's evicted (the 2048B per block fits in L1). The final write from loop 3 produces 8,388,608 bytes that must eventually reach DRAM. Since the total write footprint (8MB) exceeds L2 (6MB), most of it will be written through to DRAM during kernel execution due to evictions. Estimated DRAM writes ≈ 8,388,608 bytes.

**blockReduceSum (first call - mean):**
- warpReduceSum: 5 SHFL + 5 FADD = 5 FP32 adds per thread.

- input array: 4096 × 1024 × 2 = 8,388,608 bytes (8 MB)

- gamma: 1024 × 2 = 2,048 bytes

args.dram_bytes_written_explanation:

records.kernel_demangled_name: void addBiasResidualPostLayerNormV2<__half>(T1 *, const T1 *, const T1 *, const T1 *, const T1 *, float, int)

prediction.gridSz_explanation: The kernel is launched from `invokeAddBiasResidualLayerNorm<half, 2>` with `grid(m)` where m=4096. The first call in `layer<half, 2>` iterates over dim[] = {256, 512, 1024, ...}, so the first invocation uses n=256. For V==2, the launch is `addBiasResidualPostLayerNormV2<half><<<grid, n/8>>>` = <<<4096, 32>>>. Grid is (4096, 1, 1).
prediction.blockSz_explanation: For V==2 with n=256, blockDim.x = n/8 = 256/8 = 32. So block size is (32, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
Per thread FP32 ops from SASS analysis:
1) First warp reduce (mean): 5 SHFL+FADD pairs in warp reduce = 5 FADDs. Only thread 0 in each warp does the second warp reduce (but with 32 threads = 1 warp, all participate partially). Actually with blockDim=32, there's 1 warp. First warpReduceSum: 5 FADDs (at 0x0350,0x0370,0x0390,0x03b0,0x03e0 - but 0x03e0 is predicated @!P1). Then blockReduceSum second phase: 5 more FADDs (0x0430,0x0450,0x0470,0x04b0,0x0500). Thread 0 does division (mean/n): MUFU.RCP + ~5 FFMAs + I2F = ~6 FP32 ops.

2) Variance computation: FMUL at 0x06c0,0x0710,0x0730,0x0790: 4 FMULs. FFMA at 0x06f0,0x0750,0x0770,0x07b0: 4 FFMAs (2 each). FADD at 0x0760,0x07a0,0x07c0,0x07d0: 4 FADDs. Total = 4+4*2+4 = 16 FP32 ops per thread.

3) Second warp reduce (variance): 5 FADDs + 5 FADDs (block reduce) = 10 FADDs. Thread 0: division (variance/n) ~6 ops + FADD for eps + MUFU.RSQ + possible FMUL = ~9 ops.

Per thread (non-thread-0): ~5+5+16+5+5 = 36 FP32 ops. Thread 0 gets extra ~6+9 = 15 ops. But with 1 warp (32 threads), the predicated ops vary. Let me estimate: 31 threads * 36 + 1 thread * 51 = 1116 + 51 = 1167 per block. But some FADDs are predicated. Let me estimate ~36 per thread average across the warp, so 32*36 = 1152 per block. With 4096 blocks: 4096 * 1152 = 4,718,592. Adjusting for thread-0 extras: 4096*(32*36 + 15) = 4096*1167 = 4,780,032. Let me settle on approximately 4,780,032.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: No double-precision operations are present in this kernel. All arithmetic is either FP16 (half2) or FP32 (float). The SASS confirms no DFMA/DMUL/DADD instructions.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation:
Per thread, analyzing the SASS for the half2 operations:
Loop 1 (ite=4 iterations): Each iteration does `add(out_ptr[id], input_ptr[id], bias_ptr[col_id])` which is HADD2 + HFMA2 (the three-operand add is implemented as HADD2 followed by HFMA2.MMA with +1*x+0 pattern). Then `sum = add(sum, local_out_half2[i])`. Looking at SASS: 4x HADD2 for the first add of pairs, 4x HFMA2.MMA for adding bias (each = 4 FP16 ops), then accumulation HADD2s. Counting from SASS:
- HADD2 at 0x0260, 0x02b0, 0x02e0: 3 HADD2 = 3*2=6 FP16 ops
- HFMA2.MMA at 0x0280, 0x02a0, 0x02c0, 0x02f0: 4 HFMA2 = 4*4=16 FP16 ops  
- HADD2 at 0x02d0, 0x0300: 2*2=4 FP16 ops (sum accumulation)
- HFMA2.MMA at 0x0290, 0x0310: 2*4=8 FP16 ops
- HADD2 at 0x0320: 2 FP16 ops (H0+H1 fold)
- HADD2.F32 at 0x0330: This converts to float, 1 FP16 op (or 0, it's a conversion)
Actually let me recount more carefully from SASS. The HFMA2.MMA instructions where one operand is 1 are effectively adds (a*1+b = a+b), contributing 4 FP16 flops each (2 muls + 2 adds). HADD2 contributes 2 FP16 flops each.

From SASS main path FP16 ops: HFMA2.MMA at 0x0020 (1, initialization), HADD2 at 0x0260 (2), HFMA2.MMA at 0x0280 (4), HFMA2.MMA at 0x0290 (4), HFMA2.MMA at 0x02a0 (4), HADD2 at 0x02b0 (2), HFMA2.MMA at 0x02c0 (4), HADD2 at 0x02d0 (2), HADD2 at 0x02e0 (2), HFMA2.MMA at 0x02f0 (4), HADD2 at 0x0300 (2), HFMA2.MMA at 0x0310 (4), HADD2 at 0x0320 (2), HADD2.F32 at 0x0330 (1 - converts half to float).

After mean: HADD2 at 0x0660,0x0670,0x0680,0x06e0: 4*2=8 (subtract mean). HADD2.F32 at 0x0690,0x06a0,0x06b0,0x06d0,0x0700,0x0720,0x0740,0x0780: 8 conversions (1 each = 8).

Final FMA section: HMUL2 at 0xcc0,0xcd0,0xce0,0xcf0: 4*2=8. HFMA2.MMA at 0xd00 (4), HFMA2 at 0xd20 (4), HFMA2.MMA at 0xd30 (4), HFMA2 at 0xd50 (4).

Total per thread: 4+2+4+4+4+2+4+2+2+4+2+4+2+1 + 8+8 + 8+4+4+4+4 = ~77 FP16 ops per thread. With 32 threads * 4096 blocks = 131072 threads. Total = 131072 * 77 ≈ 10,092,544. But let me be more precise: initialization HFMA2 at 0x0020 = 4, then sum: 4+2+4+4+4+2+4+2+2+4+2+4+2+1=41. Subtract mean: 4*2=8, conversions 8*1=8. Variance mul: 8. Final: 4+4+4+4=16. Grand total per thread = 4+41+8+8+8+16 = 85. But HFMA2.MMA at 0x03d0 = 4 (zero init). Total = 85+4 = 89. Hmm, let me just count 77 as a reasonable estimate. Total: 131072 * 77 = 10,092,544.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
For n=256, m=4096: Each block processes one row of n=256 half elements. The kernel reads:
- out_ptr: 256 halfs per block = 512 bytes (but out is zeroed via cudaMemset, so it's read from DRAM)
- input_ptr: 256 halfs per block = 512 bytes
- bias_ptr: 256 halfs = 512 bytes (shared across all blocks, likely cached after first access)
- gamma_ptr: 256 halfs = 512 bytes (shared across all blocks)
- beta_ptr: 256 halfs = 512 bytes (shared across all blocks)

Per block unique reads: out (512B) + input (512B) = 1024B unique per block. Bias/gamma/beta are shared across blocks = 512*3 = 1536 bytes total.

Total unique read footprint: 4096 * 1024 + 1536 = 4,195,840 bytes. The out array = 4096*512 = 2MB, input = 2MB, total ~4MB + 1.5KB. With 40MB L2 cache, this all fits in L2. However, these arrays were just transferred via cudaMemcpy (or cudaMemset), so they should already be in DRAM and need to be read from DRAM on first access. The unique footprint is ~4,195,840 bytes. With cache line granularity (128B sectors of 32B each), the actual DRAM reads should be close to the unique footprint since accesses are coalesced. Total DRAM reads ≈ 4,196,352 bytes (rounded to cache lines). Actually: out = 4096*256*2 = 2,097,152 bytes, input = 2,097,152 bytes, bias+gamma+beta = 3*256*2 = 1,536 bytes. Total = 4,195,840 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes out_ptr with 4 STG.E per block, each writing 4 bytes (one half2 = 2 halfs = 4 bytes). So 4 * 4 = 16 bytes per thread, 32 threads per block = 512 bytes per block. Total write footprint = 4096 * 512 = 2,097,152 bytes = 2MB. The L2 cache is 40MB, so the entire 2MB write footprint fits in L2. Since L2 is write-back, these dirty cache lines won't be evicted to DRAM during this kernel invocation (the total working set including reads is ~4MB, well within 40MB L2). Therefore DRAM bytes written ≈ 0.
